top_signals.title: The Ground Beneath the Cloud: Dispersion and Dependency in the Digital Age
top_signals.summary:
Commercial cloud architecture has made digital infrastructure more resilient to localized disruption. Geographic dispersion, workload migration, and failover have allowed providers to preserve access in instances of degradation or even destruction. Yet, underpinning this resiliency are interlocking dependencies on access to energy, supply chains, and governing bodies that extend well beyond the data centers hosting the commercial cloud. The United States is building digital capacity — data centers and the underlying systems supporting them — faster than the governance frameworks needed to orchestrate the public agencies, private operators, and the physical infrastructure on which that capacity depends.
